title: Welcome home: first residents move into Orchard Fields
author: P001
summary: Catherine Ellwood's all-staff post marking the first residents moving into Orchard Fields phase 1, with thanks to the teams involved and an honest note on defects and homes still awaiting let.

blocks.p: *Published 12 October 2026 - Catherine Ellwood, Chief Executive*

On Tuesday 6 October Mark Thomas collected the keys to Flat 1, Orchard Fields - the first of our new homes at the edge of Maidstone to be let. By the end of last week a dozen households had moved in, and I spent Friday afternoon walking the scheme with Tom Lyle, Chloe Benson and some of our newest residents. Seeing a family unpack in a warm, A-rated home they can afford is the reason most of us came into housing.

blocks.h2: What Orchard Fields phase 1 gives Maidstone

bullets: **{{sql:SELECT homes FROM developments WHERE dev_id = 'DEV01'}} new homes**: {{sql:SELECT tenure_mix FROM developments WHERE dev_id = 'DEV01'}}
Air source heat pumps, solar panels and triple glazing throughout - every home is EPC A or B
Built by Castlemere Construction under a design and build contract, with {{sql:SELECT homes_england_grant_gbp FROM developments WHERE dev_id = 'DEV01'|gbp}} of Homes England grant
Phases 2 and 3 will add a further 102 homes and a community hub by 2029

blocks.p: This scheme has been four years in the making. Particular thanks go to Paul Whitaker, who has lived and breathed this site since the groundworks; to Chloe and the lettings team, who have run viewings in the evenings so working households could attend; to Kirsty Lambert for the first shared ownership reservations; and to Steve Harlow's voids team, who have been on site checking every home before handover.

blocks.h2: Being honest about what is not right yet

blocks.p: Not everything has gone to plan. Castlemere handed over the homes with a long defects list, and we will not let a home until our own team has signed it off. At the time of writing **{{fact:newbuild_awaiting_let}} homes** are still awaiting let. That costs us rent every week, but it is the right call: a resident's first week in a new home should not be spent waiting for a snagging operative.

blocks.callout: If a new Orchard Fields resident contacts you about a defect, log it in Keystone against the property with the category 'New build defect' so Paul's team can pass it to Castlemere under the defects liability period. Please do not raise it as an ordinary FieldLoop repair.
blocks.title: One ask of everyone

blocks.p: Home First is our promise that every home we provide is safe, warm and well looked after. Orchard Fields is what that looks like when we build from scratch. Our job now is to bring the same standard to the homes we have owned for twenty years. Catherine

title: Our regulatory judgement: what C2 means and what happens next
author: P001
summary: CEO message to all staff explaining the March 2026 Regulator of Social Housing judgement (C2 / G1 / V2), what it means and the improvement plan that follows.

blocks.p: *Published 26 March 2026 - Catherine Ellwood, Chief Executive*

Yesterday the Regulator of Social Housing published its judgement following the inspection of Silvering Homes in early March. I want you to hear about it from me, in plain English, before you read about it anywhere else.

rows: The highest grade. The regulator is satisfied our board and governance arrangements meet its requirements.
We meet the requirements but have less headroom than we would like to respond to adverse events - mainly because of investment in our existing homes and higher interest costs.
There are some weaknesses in how we deliver the outcomes residents should expect, and we need to improve.
table.caption: RSH judgement, March 2026

blocks.p: The regulator found that we know our homes and our residents well, that our building safety compliance is strong and that residents told inspectors our staff are kind and approachable. It also found two weaknesses that we already knew about and must now fix properly:

bullets: **Damp and mould** - we were not always investigating quickly enough, keeping residents informed or following up after works, especially at Brenchley Gardens.
**Complaint handling** - stage 1 responses were not always on time, and we were not consistently learning from complaints.

numbered: Joanne Pike has pulled together an RSH improvement action plan, which the board approved on 24 March. It is in the Board & Governance site, and every action has a named owner and a date.
Gareth Price is leading a damp and mould improvement programme ahead of Awaab's Law, which already applies to us.
Rachel Dunmore is reviewing the complaints process against the Housing Ombudsman's Complaint Handling Code, with an extra complaints officer starting in May.
The Customer Experience Committee will check our progress at every meeting, and residents on the Customer Insight Group will help us test whether things are really changing.

blocks.quote: A C2 is not a verdict on the people who work here. It is a fair description of two things we have not yet got right for residents. We will get them right.

blocks.p: I will hold two open Q&A sessions on Teams - Thursday 2 April at 12:30 and Tuesday 7 April at 16:00. Bring any question you like.

title: Copilot pilot goes live for 30 colleagues
author: P005
summary: Announcement of the Microsoft 365 Copilot pilot launching on 19 October 2026: who is in it, what it is for and the rules on vulnerability data.

version_history.change: Updated pilot numbers and support details

blocks.p: *Published 19 October 2026 - Simone Achterberg, Director of People & Change*

From today, 30 colleagues across Silvering Homes are using Microsoft 365 Copilot as part of a twelve-week pilot. Copilot is an AI assistant built into Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel and PowerPoint. It can summarise a long email thread, draft a letter, pull together notes from a Teams meeting or help analyse a spreadsheet - using only the information you already have permission to see.

bullets: The Executive Team and Joanne Pike's governance team
Six colleagues from Customer Experience, including the complaints team
Repairs planners, the damp and mould surveyors and the voids supervisor
Two housing officers and the income team leader
Finance, development and HR business partners
Craig Whitmore's IT & Data team, who will support everyone else

blocks.p: We want to know where Copilot genuinely saves time for residents' benefit - shorter waits for a stage 1 response, clearer damp and mould summaries within the Awaab's Law timescales, board papers that are ready on time - and where it does not. Pilot users will log their time savings each week and join a fortnightly show-and-tell.

Everyone in the pilot has completed the *Copilot Essentials* e-learning and signed the AI & Copilot Acceptable Use Policy. The most important rule is about the information we hold on residents' vulnerabilities and health.

blocks.callout: Copilot drafts; you decide. Never ask Copilot to list, profile or filter residents by vulnerability, health, ethnicity or other special category data, and check every draft before it reaches a resident. If Copilot shows you something you should not be able to see, stop and tell IT straight away.
blocks.title: The one rule to remember

blocks.p: Craig and his team have spent September tightening SharePoint permissions and applying sensitivity labels to libraries that hold case files, so Copilot can only show you what you are already entitled to open. If the pilot goes well, we will bring a proposal to the board in early 2027 to extend Copilot more widely. Simone

title: Expenses Policy
author: P016
summary: Rules for claiming business travel, mileage, meals and accommodation, including the 45p mileage rate, meal caps and the ban on claiming alcohol.

version_history.change: Rewritten for move to Northway Finance Cloud
Mileage rate raised from 40p to 45p per mile; meal caps updated; receipts must be photographed in the app; alcohol ban clarified

blocks.p: Silvering Homes is a charitable housing association funded mainly by residents' rents. Every pound we spend on expenses is a pound not spent on homes, so we expect colleagues to travel and spend as if it were their own money. This policy explains what you can claim, how much and how.

It applies to all employees, apprentices, agency workers engaged for more than four weeks, and non-executive board and committee members. It does not cover purchases for work (materials, tools, equipment), which must go through a purchase order.

bullets: Only claim costs you have actually incurred, wholly and necessarily, while doing Silvering business.
Use the cheapest practical option. Teams is the default for meetings between offices.
Claims must be submitted in Northway Finance Cloud within **30 days** of the expense. Claims older than 90 days will not be paid.
Every claim needs an itemised receipt, photographed in the Northway app. A card slip on its own is not a receipt.
Your line manager approves your claim; directors' claims are approved by the Chief Executive, and the Chief Executive's by the Chair.

blocks.p: Use a pool van or pool car where one is available. If you use your own vehicle for business you must have business use on your insurance and a valid MOT.

rows: Car or van - first 10,000 business miles in the tax year
HMRC approved rate. Includes fuel, wear and tear.
Car or van - over 10,000 business miles
We encourage it for town-centre visits.
Only for colleagues travelling on Silvering business.
table.caption: Mileage rates from 1 April 2026

blocks.p: You can only claim miles beyond your normal commute. If you travel from home to a resident's property and back, deduct your usual return journey to your normal base (Kingsgate House, the Aylesford depot or Linton Lodge). Record the start and end postcode and the purpose of each journey.

You can claim for a meal only when your work takes you away from your normal base and away from home for the periods below. These are maximum amounts including VAT and a reasonable tip - not allowances.

rows: You left home before 06:30 for business travel
You were away from your base for more than 5 hours, including 12:00-14:00
You returned home after 20:00, or are staying overnight
table.caption: Meal caps

blocks.callout: **Alcohol is never reimbursed** - not with a meal, not at a team celebration and not when entertaining a partner. If a receipt includes alcohol, deduct it before you claim. Claims that include alcohol will be returned unpaid.
blocks.title: No alcohol

blocks.p: Overnight stays need prior approval from your director. Book through the finance team's travel account wherever possible.

bullets: Outside London: up to £120 per night, room only
London: up to £180 per night, room only
Staying with friends or family: a flat £25 per night, no receipt needed

blocks.h1: 6. Public transport, parking and other costs

bullets: Rail: standard class, booked in advance where possible. Use a railcard if you have one.
Taxis: only when there is no reasonable alternative, for safety reasons (for example late at night) or when carrying heavy equipment. Record the reason.
Parking: claim actual cost; keep the ticket or app receipt. Parking fines and penalty charges are never reimbursed.
Training and conferences: must be approved in PeoplePath before booking.

blocks.p: Entertaining external people at Silvering's expense is rare and needs prior approval from a director. Gifts and hospitality you receive must be declared in the register held by the Head of Governance, in line with the Code of Conduct.

Finance carries out monthly sample checks of claims and reports trends to the Audit & Assurance Committee each year. A false or inflated claim is a disciplinary matter and may be gross misconduct. Over-payments will be recovered through payroll.

title: Code of Conduct
author: P013
summary: The standards of behaviour expected of every Silvering colleague and board member, including conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality, social media and relationships with residents.

version_history.change: Aligned with NHF Code of Governance 2020

blocks.h1: 1. Why we have a Code of Conduct

blocks.p: Residents trust us with their homes, their money and often very personal information. This Code sets out how we keep that trust. It applies to all staff, board and committee members, agency workers, volunteers and contractors working on our behalf. It sits alongside our values: We care, We listen and act, We take pride, and We own it.

bullets: Treat residents, colleagues and partners with courtesy, whatever the circumstances. We do not tolerate harassment, bullying or discrimination of any kind.
Respect residents' homes: show your ID badge, arrive when you said you would, and leave the home as you found it.
Never make assumptions about a resident because of their tenure, age, disability, background or the way they communicate.
If a resident is abusive or threatening, you may end the conversation or visit. Report it to your manager and record it in Keystone.

blocks.p: You must declare any interest that could, or could appear to, influence your work. Examples include a relative who is a tenant or applicant, a business interest in a supplier, or a second job with another landlord or contractor. Declarations are made on the register held by the Head of Governance & Company Secretary and are reviewed every year.
You must not take part in any decision about a lettings application, repair, complaint, contract or job application where you have a personal interest.

bullets: Never accept cash or vouchers from residents, suppliers or anyone seeking business with us.
Small tokens of thanks from residents (a box of biscuits, a card) may be accepted and shared with the team.
Any gift or hospitality worth more than **£25** must be declared on the register within 5 working days, whether accepted or declined.
Never accept hospitality from a supplier during a procurement exercise.

blocks.p: Use pool vehicles, phones, laptops and fuel cards for Silvering business only. Expenses must be claimed in line with the Expenses Policy. For example, mileage in your own car is paid at **40p per mile**, and meals only when you are working away from your base.

Only access resident and colleague records you need for your job. Looking up a neighbour, relative or a well-known person in Keystone out of curiosity is a serious breach of this Code and of data protection law. Follow the Information Security Basics guide and the AI & Copilot Acceptable Use Policy.

You are welcome to say you work for Silvering Homes. Do not post about residents, cases, complaints or colleagues, even without names, and never respond to a resident's complaint on social media - pass it to the Communications Manager. Only the Chief Executive and Communications Manager speak to the media on our behalf.

If you see something that breaches this Code, puts a resident at risk, or looks like fraud, raise it with your manager, any director or the Chair of the Audit & Assurance Committee under our Whistleblowing Policy. You will not suffer any detriment for raising a genuine concern.
Breaches of this Code will be dealt with under the Disciplinary Policy for staff and the Board Members' Code for non-executives.

title: AI & Copilot Acceptable Use Policy
author: P014
summary: Rules for using Microsoft 365 Copilot and other AI tools at Silvering, with specific controls for residents' vulnerability and special category data.

version_history.change: Approved by Executive Team for the pilot

blocks.p: This policy sets out how colleagues may use Microsoft 365 Copilot and other artificial intelligence (AI) tools for Silvering work. AI can help us respond to residents faster and write more clearly. Used carelessly, it can expose personal information, invent facts or produce letters that are wrong or unkind. This policy is about getting the benefit safely.

It applies to everyone with a Silvering Microsoft 365 account, including pilot users of Copilot from 19 October 2026, and to any AI tool used for Silvering business, including free tools on personal devices.

bullets: **Microsoft 365 Copilot** (with your Silvering login) is approved for pilot users. It works within our Microsoft 365 tenant and respects SharePoint and Teams permissions.
**Copilot Chat with the green shield** (signed in with your work account) is approved for all staff for general drafting with no personal data.
Free public AI tools (for example ChatGPT, Gemini or other chatbots signed in with a personal account) **must not** be used with any Silvering information.
New AI tools or Copilot agents must be approved by the IT & Data Manager and, where they process personal data, the Data Steering Committee.

blocks.h1: 4. Residents' vulnerability and special category data

blocks.p: We hold sensitive information about residents to deliver services safely: vulnerability flags, health and disability, safeguarding concerns, domestic abuse, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation, and criminal offence data from ASB cases. UK GDPR calls much of this *special category* data. The following rules apply in addition to our Data Protection Policy.

numbered: **Do not ask Copilot to list, filter, rank or profile residents** by vulnerability, health, disability, ethnicity or any other special category characteristic. For example, 'list all tenants with mental health flags at Brenchley Gardens' is not allowed. Reports of this kind must come from Keystone through the approved Power BI reports.

**Do not paste vulnerability or health details into prompts** unless it is essential to the task in front of you (for example, adjusting the tone of a single letter to a resident with a learning disability) and then include only the minimum.

**Never put special category data into a document, email or chat that is shared more widely than it needs to be.** Copilot can surface anything you can open. If a summary contains vulnerability information, check who it will be shared with before sending.

**Safeguarding referrals, domestic abuse case notes and Careline records must not be summarised or drafted with Copilot** during the pilot. These libraries are labelled *Highly Confidential* and excluded from Copilot.

**Decisions about residents remain human decisions.** Copilot must not be used to decide priority, eligibility, enforcement action, compensation or the outcome of a complaint. It may help you draft the explanation once a person has decided.

If Copilot shows you information about a resident or colleague that you should not be able to see, **stop, do not share it, and report it to the IT Service Desk** within 24 hours. This is treated as a near miss, not a disciplinary matter.

bullets: You are responsible for anything you send, whoever drafted it.
Check every fact, date and number against the source system - Copilot can make things up.
Letters to residents must follow the Plain-English Writing Guide and the resident letter template.
Board and committee papers drafted with Copilot must say so on the cover paper.

blocks.p: Tell attendees at the start of a meeting if it is being recorded or transcribed. Do not transcribe meetings with residents, safeguarding or case conferences, disciplinary or grievance hearings, or legal advice sessions.

Deliberate misuse - for example, using Copilot to look up information about a neighbour, or pasting resident data into a public AI tool - will be dealt with under the Disciplinary Policy and may be reported to the ICO.

kv: April 2027, or at the end of the pilot

title: Information Security Basics
author: P014
summary: A short guide to keeping Silvering systems and resident data safe: passwords and MFA, phishing, devices, sharing files and reporting incidents.

blocks.h1: Ten things every colleague must do

numbered: Use a passphrase of at least 14 characters for your Silvering account, and never reuse it anywhere else.
Approve multi-factor authentication (MFA) prompts only when you are signing in yourself. An unexpected prompt means someone has your password - report it.
Lock your screen (Windows key + L) whenever you leave your desk, including at the depot and Linton Lodge.
Keep resident information in Keystone, FieldLoop and SharePoint - not on your desktop, a USB stick or personal email.
Share files with a link to a named person rather than 'anyone with the link'.
Check the sensitivity label before you share: Public, Internal, Confidential or Highly Confidential.
Think before you click. Hover over links and check the sender's address.
Never give your password to anyone, including IT. We will never ask for it.
Report a lost or stolen phone or laptop to the Service Desk immediately, day or night.
Report any data breach - an email to the wrong person, a lost letter, a document left in a resident's home - to the IT Service Desk within 24 hours.

blocks.p: Most attacks on housing associations start with an email. Common tricks we have seen this year include fake invoices from suppliers asking us to change bank details, fake Microsoft sign-in pages and messages that appear to come from the Chief Executive asking for gift cards.

rows: 'Please process this today and don't mention it to finance'
A supplier asks us to pay into a new account - always phone the supplier on a number we already hold
A link to 'view a shared document' that asks for your password again

blocks.p: Use the **Report** button in Outlook to send suspicious emails to IT. Do not forward them to colleagues.

bullets: Keep your tablet locked and in your possession. Do not let residents use it.
Do not photograph documents, medication or personal items unless it is necessary for the job (for example, evidence of damp and mould) - and then only the area you need.
Photos go straight into FieldLoop, not your camera roll.

blocks.p: We must report serious personal data breaches to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware of them, so speed matters. Report first, explain later. Contact the IT Service Desk on extension 4400 or servicedesk@silvering-homes.org.uk.

title: Safeguarding Adults and Children Policy - staff summary
author: P011
summary: A two-page summary of the Safeguarding Adults and Children Policy: what safeguarding means at Silvering, signs to look for, and exactly what to do if you have a concern.

blocks.p: Our operatives, surveyors, housing officers and contact centre advisers are often the only professionals who see inside a resident's home. That means we may be the first to notice that a child or an adult is being harmed or is at risk. You do not need to be sure, and you do not need to investigate. You need to notice, record and report.

bullets: Unexplained injuries, or a resident who seems frightened of someone in the household
A home in very poor condition: severe hoarding, no heating or food, or signs of self-neglect
Children who seem unsupervised, hungry or out of school during the day
Someone else controlling the resident's money, phone or contact with us
Signs of cuckooing - a vulnerable resident's home taken over by others, often for drug dealing
Damp and mould in a home where there is a baby, an older person or someone with a respiratory condition, where the resident is not able to report it themselves

numbered: If someone is in immediate danger, call **999**.
Make sure you and the resident are safe. Do not confront an alleged abuser.
Write down what you saw and heard, in the person's own words, with the date and time.
Tell a Designated Safeguarding Officer **the same working day** (Nadia Rahman, Margaret Ogunleye or Owen Fletcher), or the duty manager out of hours.
Complete the safeguarding concern form in Keystone. The DSO will decide whether to make a referral to the county council's adult or children's services.

blocks.callout: Do not promise a resident that you will keep what they tell you secret. Explain that you may need to share it to keep them or others safe.
blocks.title: Confidentiality

blocks.p: Safeguarding records are kept in the restricted safeguarding area of Keystone and the Highly Confidential safeguarding library. They must not be copied into general case notes, emails, Teams chats or Copilot prompts.
All staff complete safeguarding awareness training at induction and every two years. Frontline staff complete the enhanced module every year. Training records are held in PeoplePath.

title: Plain-English Writing Guide for resident letters
author: P003
summary: Practical guidance and before-and-after examples for writing letters and emails residents understand first time, including damp and mould and complaint responses.

blocks.p: One in six adults in England has very poor literacy skills, and many of our residents speak English as a second language. Our Tenant Satisfaction Measures show that residents who feel kept informed are much more likely to be satisfied overall. A clear letter prevents a phone call, a complaint and, sometimes, an Ombudsman case.

numbered: Put the most important thing first.
Keep sentences to 15-20 words on average.
Use 'we' and 'you'.
Use active verbs: 'we will fix your boiler', not 'the boiler will be repaired'.
Give a real date and time, not 'shortly' or 'in due course'.
Explain what the resident needs to do in a separate, clear section.
Say sorry plainly if we got something wrong. Do not say 'we apologise for any inconvenience'.
Avoid jargon and abbreviations (see the swap list).
Never blame the resident for damp and mould or suggest it is their 'lifestyle'.
Read it aloud before you send it.

blocks.h1: Before and after: damp and mould

blocks.quote: Further to the inspection undertaken at the above property on the 14th inst., please be advised that the surveyor has identified condensation-related mould growth. Tenants are advised to ventilate adequately. Remedial works will be scheduled in due course.

Thank you for letting Ellie Novak into your home on 14 October. Ellie found mould in your bedroom and bathroom. This is caused by moisture that cannot escape, because the extractor fan in your bathroom is not working well enough. We will fit a new fan and treat the mould on 21 October between 8am and 12pm. Ellie will call you two weeks later to check it has worked.

blocks.p: When we investigate a significant damp and mould hazard, we must send the resident a written summary within **3 working days** of the investigation. It must say what we found, whether there is a significant hazard, what we will do and when, and what happens if we cannot do it in time. Use the damp and mould summary template in the Repairs & Maintenance site.

Every stage 1 reply must answer each point the resident raised, say clearly whether we have upheld the complaint, explain what we will do to put it right, and tell them how to escalate to stage 2 and to the Housing Ombudsman.

title: Doorstep - resident magazine, Autumn 2026
author: P037
summary: The autumn 2026 edition of Doorstep, sent to every household: damp and mould advice, winter readiness, Orchard Fields, our TSM results and how residents can get involved.

blocks.p: Welcome to the autumn edition of Doorstep. In March the Regulator of Social Housing told us that we need to get better at dealing with damp and mould and with complaints. You told us the same thing in our satisfaction survey. This edition explains what we are changing, and how you can hold us to it. - Catherine Ellwood, Chief Executive

blocks.h1: Damp and mould: tell us early

blocks.p: Damp and mould is not your fault, and we want to know about it. From October 2025 the law changed so that landlords must investigate serious damp and mould within 10 working days and start safety works within 5 working days of the investigation. We now have two specialist surveyors and a dedicated damp team.

bullets: Report it on MySilvering, by phone on 01622 000 400, or tell any Silvering colleague who visits
Take a photo if you can - it helps us decide how quickly to come
We will write to you within 3 working days of our visit to tell you what we found and what we will do
Bleed your radiators and check your boiler pressure - videos on MySilvering
Know where your stop tap is
Struggling with energy bills? Our money advice team can help with grants and the Warm Home Discount
SilverLiving residents: your coordinator will call you in November to check you are ready

blocks.h1: Our new homes at Orchard Fields

blocks.p: The first residents moved into our 62 new homes at Orchard Fields in October. Every home has a heat pump and solar panels. Phase 2 is being built now.

blocks.h1: How did we do? Your satisfaction survey results

blocks.p: Last year {{fact:tsm_overall_2526}} of tenants were satisfied with our service overall, and {{fact:tsm_repairs_2526}} with our repairs service. But only {{fact:tsm_complaints_2526}} of people who complained were satisfied with how we handled it. That is not good enough, and our new complaints team is working to change it.

Join the Customer Insight Group, take part in a scrutiny review, or become a Street Champion on your estate. Contact Grace Osei, Resident Involvement & Insight Officer, on 01622 000 455 or getinvolved@silvering-homes.org.uk. We pay for your time with shopping vouchers and cover travel and childcare costs.
